correctness.rationale: The origin monitored-step model is the same as the full-text source. The existing matrix resolvent yields scalar survival GF algebraically; explicit even-time singular transfer gives sharp first-return survival and hit tails and infinite mean. Exact coefficient expansion has a uniform summable factorial bound in the joint limit, identified by Laplace transforms with the Bessel law; conditioning uses S_2=p-p^2/2 and Bessel derivative yields a probability density. Independently implemented exact rational Markov propagation, Fourier inversion and numeric asymptotic tests passed 215 checks. Limit proofs are analytic, not experimental.

originality.rationale: The 2025 preprint/2026 paper provides the model, exact resolvent and all-parameter recurrence (not new here). The new claim concerns a uniform simultaneous vanishing-noise/long-time coefficient asymptotic with explicit conditional Bessel law plus an infinite-mean threshold. Its proof performs a nontrivial, factorially dominated joint limit absent from the inspected source. Compared primary work addresses unmonitored return, a distinct channel, or a different observable. Risk: classical persistent-walk first-passage theorems or direct asymptotic analysis of the existing generating function may cover some or all of the claim.
residual_risks: A Bessel rare-switching **position** law and absorption formulas for a different correlated walk are already present in Konno (2009); a reduction through that literature could conceivably imply this boundary-layer law.
The exact first-return generating function in Štefaňák et al. implies all coefficient formulas; the contribution is explicitly limited to derived asymptotics and singular conditional law.
Classical telegraph/persistent-walk absorption or general two-variable analytic combinatorics could implicitly contain an equivalent Bessel first passage scaling; no blanket novelty is asserted.
Independent external peer assessment is outstanding.

value.rationale: The existing literature notes nonuniformity near zero noise but does not quantify what happens to the O(p) exceptional trajectories: here they exhibit a specific t~p^-1 conditional survival law with heavy tail, while E[T] jumps from 2 at p=0 to infinity at every p>0. This motivates the precise boundary-layer analysis as a timing/detection phenomenon, not a mere numerical constant or rebranding of recurrence.
